svg.text: ECS r3 — MECHANISM, MEASURED: UPRIGHT → RIDING (TENSION-SHORTENING, AS DOCUMENTED)
Riding = pelvis 15° + spinal flexion 20° about L3 (35° lean). A6 (hidden in the shell and the back panel) holds the A1 hubs a fixed distance (along the back) above the A4 stud;
flexion lengthens the back between them, so the load body slides down the trunk over the A4 stud in the rail's S3 slot. Same scale, same hip centre H, load COM at the load body's centre (8 kg).
100 mm · scale 1:6.9 on A3 · grey dot = A4 stud (pelvis) · hollow = COM with the mechanism locked
Slide of the load body on the A4 stud
…its source: back elongation, A4 stud → A1 hubs
Slot travel available (S3, the A4 slot)
the slide moves the COM back along the leaning trunk
shoulder-strap front run shortening, same lean
Reading: at a realistic riding lean the back lengthens about 12 mm between the
A4 stud and the A1 hubs, so the documented tension-shortening mechanism slides
the load body by that much. The documentation's 100–150 mm drop and 30–40 %
moment-arm reduction (labelled 'conceptual targets' on its kinematic sheet)
are not reached by strap geometry; most of the lever change between walking
and riding comes from the posture itself.
targets: kinematic sheet p09, which labels them 'conceptual targets for visualisation'
slide over the A4 stud, 20° flexion
horizontal lever change from the posture alone: 40.4 % (not the product)
measured 0.0 mm: the slide runs parallel to the rail
